figures.cap: cross-section of pipe with water of width 20 cm and depth d

parts.latex:
A cylindrical pipe with a radius of 12.5 cm is filled with water to a depth, $d$ cm, as shown.

The surface of the water has a width of 20 cm.

\exfigure{300_q12_1}

What is the depth of water in the pipe?

solutions.latex:
The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so the half-width of the water surface is $10$ cm.

Let $h$ be the distance from the centre to the surface. In the right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $12.5$ (the radius), Pythagoras' theorem gives
$$\begin{aligned} h^2 + 10^2 &= 12.5^2\\ h^2 &= 156.25 - 100 = 56.25\\ h &= 7.5 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
From the figure the centre is above the water surface, so the depth is the radius minus $h$:
$$\begin{aligned} d &= 12.5 - 7.5\\ &= 5.0 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
This is option B.

Hence calculate the approximate area of the lake, to the nearest square metre.

solutions.latex:
The grassed section has parallel sides 160, 150 and 250 with strip width 100, so apply the trapezoidal rule twice.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 100\times(160+150) + \dfrac{1}{2}\times 100\times(150+250) \\ &= 50\times 310 + 50\times 400 \\ &= 35\,500 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total area} &= 200\times 250 + \dfrac{1}{2}\times\pi\times 100^2 \\ &= 65\,707.96\ldots \\ &\approx 65\,708 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
The lake is the total area less the grassed section.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Lake area} &= 65\,708 - 35\,500 \\ &= 30\,208 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
A container for soccer balls is made using two half spheres joined to each end of a cylindrical body.

\exfigure{40_q34_1}

Three soccer balls fit exactly inside the container. Each ball has a diameter of 23 cm.

The hemispherical ends of the container just touch the surface of the soccer balls.

What is the total surface area of the container? Give your answer in square metres correct to 1 decimal place.

solutions.latex:
The container is a sphere's surface (two hemispheres, radius $\dfrac{23}{2}$ cm) plus the curved surface of a cylinder of the same radius and length $2\times 23=46$ cm (two balls).

$$\text{Surface area of sphere}=4\pi\left(\dfrac{23}{2}\right)^2$$

$$\text{Curved surface of cylinder}=2\pi\times\dfrac{23}{2}\times(23\times 2)$$

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore\ \text{Total surface area} &= 4\pi\left(\dfrac{23}{2}\right)^2+2\pi\times\dfrac{23}{2}\times 46 \\ &= 4985.707\ldots \text{ cm}^2 \\ &\approx 4985.7 \text{ cm}^2 \\ &\approx 0.5 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

The total surface area is $0.5 \text{ m}^2$ (1 decimal place).
criteria: Finds the total surface area, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The volume of 30 spheres is
$$\begin{aligned} V &= \dfrac{4}{3} \times \pi \times 1.5^3 \times 30 \\ &= 424.115\ldots \text{ cm}^3 \end{aligned}$$
The pyramid volume is the volume of the spheres plus the empty space:
$$\begin{aligned} V_{\text{pyramid}} &= 424.115\ldots + 634 \\ &= 1058.115\ldots \text{ cm}^3 \end{aligned}$$
Using $V = \dfrac{1}{3}Ah$:
$$\begin{aligned} 1058.115 &= \dfrac{1}{3} \times (14 \times 14) \times h \\ h &= \dfrac{1058.115 \times 3}{14 \times 14} \\ &\approx 16.2 \text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ h = 16 \text{ cm (to the nearest whole number)}$$
criteria: Provides evidence of equating volumes to find $h$, or equivalent merit

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Maximum floor area} &= 70\%\times 569 \\ &= 398.3 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
